Alex.confusing: Mostly nothing, though it was unclear how much a lone Tit's claim could counter a Floofer who lied about the same role. Tit and Floofer both visiting Blair was hard to untangle.
Alex.fun: Catching Drew's lie in round 1 with my Falcon read and getting the table to act on it quickly.
Alex.change: Give the early game less runaway scoring. Blair's one big round-1 win made the standings feel decided before round 2.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed Pigeon and said I visited Finley, but Finley had no egg, and that was easy to check. As the Floofer I should have claimed a role with no visible effect, like Kookaburra or Hawk, or hugged someone who would back me up. In round 1 I also threw three high cards, including the 13, on a vote that was already lopsided. I should have kept some.

Blair.confusing: Nothing major. The one thing I had to puzzle over was how Turkey and Falcon eggs combine in the nest counts, since players kept misreading them.
Blair.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx. Steering the table onto Drew, a Farm player, with a Meowfia win and a 12-point banked card felt great.
Blair.change: Show Meowfia some hint of their partner, or give them a way to coordinate. Playing alone as Meowfia was hard to do deliberately.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards, including my 13, at Alex, who turned out to be Farm. I lost the 13 when the round was lost. I should have kept my high cards, since I was far ahead and the Falcon read gave me no real evidence.

Casey.confusing: How the Tit's egg and the nest-size changes should be read, and whether Meowfia in round 3 could lie convincingly about visitor lists. In round 1 my own +1 was read as evidence against me.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when the Kookaburra confirmation of Blair as Falcon and the Turkey egg math lined up. We caught the Meowfia Alex cleanly.
Casey.change: Give players a bit more information about how their own role's result is reported, for example whether a Tit hit is clearly shown. Also add some catch-up for players who fall behind, since Blair's early lead was nearly decisive.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I accepted Ellis's Eagle claim and threw two high cards at Alex. Ellis wasn't verified, and Drew's claim of Tit was suspicious. I should have thrown fewer cards, or at Drew. In round 1 I also threw four cards, including the W8, when my confidence was only moderate.

Drew.confusing: Turkey's visitor eggs go to the visitor's nest, not mine, so the egg math wasn't clear. I also wasn't sure what a Turkey is allowed to know about who visited.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when I was the Floofer and Alex, who was really Farm, took the whole eggsecution. I then banked 16 points with a bluff Tit claim, which got me to second place.
Drew.change: Give a few roles a way to confirm themselves, or reduce how much one big early score decides the game. Blair's 16 in round 1 was almost impossible to catch.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I said "nobody visited me" as a flat fact, as if I knew it. A Turkey can't know that, and the claim got me eggsecuted. I should have said "I didn't see any visitors, but I'd have heard about eggs in other nests."

Ellis.confusing: Nothing major, but it was unclear whether a Turkey's own egg counts could confirm anything, and I misread how Blair's +2 worked in round 2.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I banked 18 points with two big cards in a winning throw. Round 1, when I played the Mouser and Drew took the fall, was fun too.
Ellis.change: Give each player a way to confirm a claim. A lone Eagle or Owl read is easy to misjudge, and the table herds onto one target.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw H12, H10 and H6 at Alex on a guess. Alex and Drew both claimed Tit, so one of them was the Floofer, and I picked Alex. Drew was the Floofer. I should have kept my big cards and thrown a low card, or thrown at Drew.

Finley.confusing: Nothing was badly unclear, but it took me a while to see how heavily the scoring favors banking big throws on winning rounds. Blair's lead from round 1 was already close to decisive.
Finley.fun: Piecing together the Owl, Eagle and Tit claims in round 3 to narrow the Floofer down to two players. The round 1 Eagle and Tit cross-check was fun too.
Finley.change: Make comebacks more realistic. One big early win put Blair out of reach, so the later rounds felt like they didn't matter for first place.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw three high cards at Alex on a roughly 50/50 guess, and Alex was Farm. I should have thrown low cards, or noticed that Drew guessed Owl on Blair, which fits a Floofer bluffing, and thrown at Drew instead.

review.title: The Honest Turkey
review.headline: An honest Turkey was eggsecuted, then Blair's banked 12 and 28 decided everything.
review.summary: Round 1 set the pattern. The table piled onto Drew, a truthful Turkey, because of a wording slip and a bad Tit claim. Meowfia Blair banked a 12 and led from then on. In round 2 the table correctly caught Alex's false Pigeon claim, and Blair banked 28 more. That made her lead nearly unbeatable. In round 3 Drew, the lone Floofer, copied the Tit claim and sat out a coin flip between himself and Alex. The table picked wrong. Blair won the game with 45.

rounds.recap: Drew, a truthful Turkey, said nobody visited him. Turkeys do not learn visitors, so this looked like a lie once Alex's Falcon read showed Casey had visited. Casey wrongly claimed his +1 egg was a Tit hit, but it was Drew's Turkey egg. Casey's claim muddied the math, and Finley read it backwards. Everyone but the two Meowfia threw at Drew. Blair (Sphinx) and Ellis (Mouser) won, and Blair banked a 12.

Alex (Floofer) claimed Pigeon and said he visited Finley, but Finley got no egg. Blair's +2 was explained by a Falcon egg plus a Turkey egg from visiting Ellis. Ellis briefly misread his own Turkey, then backed off. The table threw at Alex. Farm won, and Blair banked 28, pulling far ahead.

Casey's Owl and Ellis's Eagle both showed Casey, Drew and Alex visited Blair as Owl, Floofer and Tit. Drew (the Floofer) and Alex both claimed Tit. The table had no tiebreaker and followed Ellis's elimination logic onto Alex, who was the real Tit. Meowfia won with Drew's 16. Blair was already uncatchable.

highlights.text: Drew's Turkey math was exactly right, that Casey's +1 couldn't also be a Tit hit. Finley used the same fact to condemn him, and an honest player went down.
Finley, a hidden Meowfia, spotted that Alex's Pigeon claim contradicted his own +0 and led the vote at his own teammate. He then threw one cheap card at Drew for the consolation.
Drew, the real Floofer, claimed Tit and guessed Owl on Blair. That was a convincing bluff, built to match Casey's public Owl claim. It pulled the table into a coin flip.
Casey's Owl list (Eagle, Floofer, Tit) and Ellis's Eagle list gave a real puzzle. The Floofer had to be Alex or Drew, and the table got it wrong.

confusions.what: Said nobody visited him, forgetting that a Turkey can't tell who visited him. This looked like a lie and sank him.
Claimed his Tit guess of House Cat hit and gave him the egg. The egg actually came from Drew's Turkey, and a Tit hit would have made him +2.
Accused Drew of lying about visitors, though a Turkey learns nothing about who visits.
Argued Casey's +1 meant Drew was House Cat. That reverses the logic: +1 fits Drew's Turkey egg alone, and Casey's Tit claim was the thing that didn't add up.
Said Blair lied about visiting him because he was +0. A Turkey gains no eggs from visitors, only lays them.
Claimed Pigeon and said he visited Finley with no egg. A Pigeon lays an egg in its target, so Finley's +0 contradicted him.
Reasoned that her lack of an egg meant Ellis visited someone. She was hugged, so her Falcon did nothing, and her dawn report never said so.
Named Alex as the Floofer 'by elimination' while ignoring that Alex could be the real Tit and Drew the Floofer.

worked: Egg-count cross-checks. Alex's false Pigeon claim in round 2 was caught because Finley's +0 contradicted it. The +2 on Blair was explained by Falcon plus Turkey.
Owl and Eagle visitor lists in round 3 created a real puzzle. Two players could claim Tit, and the table had to pick between them.
Throwing for the consolation. Finley and Alex both threw one low or high card at the other team to get a card back. This was a sensible, visible decision.
Hug on a Falcon hid the Falcon's result. Blair's missing report in round 3 was ambiguous in a good way.
problems: Banking a winning throw at full value makes one round decide the game. Blair banked 12, then 28, and led 45 to 24 or less. The final round had no race, since nest cards are worth only 1. Fix: cap the cards banked per round, or catch up the loser.

Many night actions were arbitrary visits with no useful result. Most players had no information to choose a target. Round 1 had few informative nights, and the Mouser wink was never used. Fix: give every role a reason to pick a target, or tell players who is in play.
A Turkey cannot learn who visited. An honest Turkey that says 'nobody visited me' sounds like a liar, and this killed Drew in round 1. Fix: make the Turkey report its visitors, or reword the role.

Hugging gives no dawn feedback, and the Sphinx's hug was 'no effect at tier 50'. Players cannot tell a hug from a quiet night, and tier language is not explained. Fix: tell hugged players, or explain what the tier means.

Round 3 had one Meowfia and two Tit claims, and no information could separate them. The vote was a coin flip, and the table's Eagle and Owl info did not settle it. Fix: let the Tit's result be checkable, or add a role that can check Tit claims.
